text: [serious, cinematic storyteller, brisk pace] Ninety-nine out of every hundred will die for it. And every one of them believes he'll be the one who survives. They came from every direction. Trucks, carts, whole families carrying shovels. Two friends from the same street dug side by side. On the first day, they shared their water. On the second day, they marked their ground with rope. On the third day, only one of them came back. Fathers stopped trusting their sons. Brothers stopped speaking. Then the soldiers came to guard the gold. And the soldiers fought each other. Every night, the camp grew a little quieter. Sandals left at tent doors. Shovels no one came back for. Fourteen centuries ago, the Prophet said people would fight over it. And ninety-nine of every hundred would be killed. Each one hoping... to be the one who lived. When the dust settled, the gold was still there. It didn't care who owned it. And far from the river, in a city no one was watching, a man was giving wealth away... without even counting it. And people had started to whisper a name.
